before: Triton rejected int1 values for an int8 block pointer store
cause: Logical predicates use i1, but Triton boolean memory uses byte storage. Block-pointer loads now convert bytes to predicates and stores convert predicates to bytes at the serialization boundary.
reference_difference: Triton's scalar/tensor-pointer store converts bool pointers and values to int8. Our block-pointer form instead explicitly cast the value to int1, which the external compiler rejects. The change is mechanical type representation, not a new algorithm or physical program structure.
